cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, starts building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. The spot is Mount Moriah. And friend, this isn't some random lot he found scrolling his phone at midnight.

cards.question: Solomon builds the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah. What had happened on that mountain before?

answers.text: The LORD had appeared to David there
David had been anointed king there

cards.question: Solomon's building spot is the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, a place already prepared by ___.

cards.text: Solomon breaks ground on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. The foundation goes down sixty cubits long and twenty wide, by the old standard.

Then the GOLD starts: the inside of the portico, the main room, the beams, the thresholds, the walls with cherubim carved on them, even the DOORS. Friend, the fanciest thing in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

Then comes the Most Holy Place, twenty cubits by twenty, and the inside alone gets six HUNDRED talents of fine gold. In there, Solomon makes two cherubim of sculptured work and overlays them with gold too.

cards.question: Each of the two cherubim in the Most Holy Place stretches out two wings. One wing touches the temple wall, and the other touches the ___ of the other cherub.
True or false: Wing to wing, the two cherubim reach all the way across the Most Holy Place, from wall to wall.

cards.text: The two cherubim stand on their feet, facing the main room. Then Solomon makes the veil from blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen.

cards.question: Cherubim carved on the walls, two golden cherubim in the Most Holy Place. What does Solomon weave into the veil?

cards.text: Out front, he makes two pillars, thirty-five cubits high together, each with a five-cubit capital on top. He puts chainwork on top and fastens a hundred pomegranates into it.
He sets the pillars up in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. Then he does something for them that the Millers once did for my handle.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon gives each of the two pillars in front of the temple a name.
One of the pillar names also belongs to the man who married Ruth (Ruth 4:13). Which two names does Solomon give the pillars?

cards.text: Now the furnishings, starting with a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty wide and ten HIGH. Friend, I'm a stamper on a little gold base, and I'd need a LADDER just to see the top of this thing.
Then he makes the Sea of cast metal: round, ten cubits rim to rim, five high, with two rows of ox figures cast right below the rim. Not the Tub, not the Big Bowl, the SEA.

cards.question: The Sea doesn't sit on the ground. It rests on twelve ___, three facing each direction.

cards.text: The Sea holds three thousand baths. Then Solomon makes ten basins for washing, five on the south side and five on the north, and the parts of the burnt offering get rinsed in them.

cards.question: The ten basins are for rinsing the parts of the burnt offering. So who uses the Sea for washing?
True or false: Solomon makes ten gold lampstands and puts all ten together on the north side of the temple.
Solomon also makes ten tables for the temple. Like the basins and the lampstands, they go five on the south side and five on the ___ side.

cards.text: Add a hundred gold bowls, then the courtyard of the priests and the large court, with bronze on the doors. The Sea goes in at the southeast corner.

Huram, the craftsman the king of Tyre sent (2 Chronicles 2:13), finishes his work: the pillars, the network, four hundred pomegranates, the stands, the basins, the Sea and its oxen, the pots, shovels and forks, all polished bronze. They're cast in clay molds on the plain of the Jordan.

cards.question: Solomon makes all these bronze articles in great abundance. What's the result?

answers.text: No one could figure out the weight
It used up every mine in Israel

cards.text: Bronze outside, gold inside: Solomon makes the golden altar and the tables for the house of God. Friend, the only gold I own is the base I'm standing on, and I am NOT stepping off it.

cards.question: What gets placed on the tables Solomon makes for the house of God?
True or false: The lampstands of pure gold and their lamps burn out in the large court.

cards.text: Last comes the rest in purest gold: flowers, lamps, tongs, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, censers, and the gold doors to the Most Holy Place and the main hall. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage is temple building plans and furnishings, including measurements, materials, item lists and placement. The docs name 'building plans, like the tabernacle or the temple' as a long stretch that gets one summary card and no choice cards. The docs also say a stretch never gets a stop of its own. The walkthrough instead gives this material two full stops with 14 choice cards, on details like the cherubim wings, the pillar names, the oxen under the Sea and the sides the lampstands and tables stand on.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a long stretch, like 2 Chronicles 3-4 (temple building plans), should it still get normal stops with choice cards on its details? Or should it be treated as a long stretch, and if so, how is Prep built when there is nothing else in the passage to ask about?

findings.problem: The setup inside the question ('One of the pillar names also belongs to the man who married Ruth') points straight to Boaz. Only the right answer contains Boaz, so the hint rules out both wrong answers without the baker knowing the pillar names at all.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Story card 4 already told the baker that the basins go five on the south side and five on the north. The question then says the tables go 'Like the basins and the lampstands,' so the blank (north) was given away by an earlier story card.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card carries three separate moments: the hundred gold bowls, the two courts with bronze doors, and the Sea being placed at the southeast corner.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'Bronze outside, gold inside' is a storyteller line that adds a fact the text doesn't state. The passage never says the bronze items were all outside or that the gold items were all inside.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: Many story cards read as a flat list of facts with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are stop 1 cards 4, 6, 9 and 11, and stop 2 cards 4, 8 and 9. With so much measurement and material detail, these stretches read like a chore to get through.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
